'''Uchi Shrine''' (うちじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Gojo, Nara Prefecture. It is an Engishiki major shrine, and its former shrine rank was gōsha.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Kuniumi Myōjin
* Uchi no Omi ancestral deity Hikofutooshi Makoto no Omi (imperial prince of Emperor Kōgen)
* Uchi-do no Mitama Haniyasu-no-Kami

=== History ===
Its foundation is presumed to be older than the adjacent temple Anshō-ji. According to old documents of Anshō-ji, En no Gyōja was training on Mount Katsuragi and wondered at a light that shone every night; when he visited this place, he encountered the source of the light, Kuniumi Myōjin, and, moved by the deity's will to care for and worry for the country, founded Shinkōzan Kunishō-ji, the present Shinkōzan Anshō-ji. Therefore, it is thought that when Shinkōzan Anshō-ji was founded, a sacred seat of Kuniumi Myōjin already existed at Uchi Shrine, or at least at the location of Uchi Shrine. The founding of Anshō-ji is said to date to the era of Emperor Jitō, around the end of the Asuka period. The annual festival is on October 17.

=== Man'yōshū ===
:[https://sunagoya.com/tanka/?p=20042 Tamakiharu, in the great plain of <ruby>Uchi<rt>うち</rt></ruby>, lining up horses]
:[https://sunagoya.com/tanka/?p=20042 They tread at dawn, that deep grassy field (<ruby>Nakatsu Sumeramikoto<rt>なかつすめらみこと</rt></ruby>, Man'yōshū)]

=== Precincts ===
Haiden, Norito-den, and Shinden
The sacred image (height 23.5 cm) is a single-block carved seated figure with polychrome robes and formal headdress, hands folded (Muromachi period)
The shinden is an unpainted one-bay shrine
